_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.

themes.title: Canada-US trade war LIVE — Section 338 50% tariffs operative since Aug 22; Canada confirmed Sept 8 retaliation (steel, dairy, appliances, ag equipment, pulp/paper, electronics); USTR Greer says no new talks planned
themes.summary: As of August 24, the Canada-US trade war has entered its next escalatory phase. The 50% Section 338 tariff on approximately $20 billion of Canadian-origin goods — motor vehicles, dairy, alcoholic beverages, cement, furniture, clothing, and a wide Annex II list including hockey sticks, plywood, seeds, fishing rods, and wigs — took effect at 12:01am ET on Saturday August 22, 2026, after talks collapsed on the night of August 21. On Saturday August 22, Prime Minister Carney addressed Canadians publicly and confirmed that Canada's retaliatory tariffs will take effect September 8 — the Tuesday after Labor Day — targeting US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics on a dollar-for-dollar basis. Carney said 'in the coming days, we will release the details of these new tariff measures,' meaning the specific product-level list (HTS lines and rates) remains forthcoming but the sector scope is now known. USTR Jamieson Greer told Fox News on August 22 that 'no new talks are planned with Canada' and that the US would be 'moving forward with measures that respond to Canadian retaliation,' suggesting a counter-retaliation response to Canada's Sept 8 action is possible, potentially beginning an escalation spiral. Greer framed the breakdown as Canada's fault, stating 'they've always had the best deal, and they still would have an even better deal, but they didn't want that.' Carney stated Canada 'cannot accept what they have offered, and will not give what they have asked,' characterizing Canada's position as 'at war' after getting attacked. Trade legal experts note that both sides have now publicly committed to positions from which retreat would be politically costly, increasing the probability that escalation becomes structural rather than tactical. The retaliatory scope — US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp/paper, electronics — is broad enough to create pass-through inflation risk in Canada and meaningful export disruption for affected US industries, particularly in US farm states and manufacturing corridors. Section 338 carries no fixed statutory expiry and remains operative indefinitely unless the President acts. The USMCA formal review with Canada has not commenced; US-Mexico USMCA review is advancing separately. The September 8 Canada retaliation effective date is now the dominant near-term binary for CAD crosses, ahead of the Warsh Jackson Hole keynote on August 28 and the September 11 US CPI print.

implications.CAD: MAXIMUM CAD negative shock sustained: tariffs operative since Aug 22, retaliation confirmed for Sept 8 with sector scope now known. USDCAD bulls target 1.4248 (MNI/Jun 24-30 high bull trigger) as next major resistance above 1.4100. The structural USDCAD trend remains bullish; 50-day EMA near 1.4017-1.4021 is critical support. USTR Greer's 'no new talks planned' statement materially reduces near-term resolution probability. Sept 8 retaliation effective date could bring further CAD pressure if US counter-retaliates (Greer signalled this). Canada's pass-through inflation from 50% tariff on $20B of goods is CAD-negative via growth/BoC easing expectations. Automotive sector disruption most severe given 50% duty on Canadian motor vehicles with no CUSMA exemption.
implications.USD: USDCAD directionally bullish from tariff shock, but broad USD direction dominated by Warsh Jackson Hole Aug 28 and Treasury buyback-driven yield suppression. DXY ~98.80-98.99, softened by Treasury doubling buybacks to at least $32B/quarter. Canada shock adds modest USD safe-haven bid vs commodity bloc but does not materially alter DXY path which is primarily a Fed/rate differential story.
implications.MXN: USMCA credibility damage from US-Canada rupture adds uncertainty to the US-Mexico track. Mexico-specific tariff tracks advancing more smoothly and separately. Modest USDMXN risk premium from contagion.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EURCAD likely bid on CAD weakness. Broader protectionism escalation signal from first-ever invocation of Section 338 has limited but non-zero EUR contagion via trade policy risk premium.
implications.AUD: Commodity-bloc contagion — AUD trades defensively in acute CAD-shock episodes. AUDUSD at multi-month highs near 0.7170 but vulnerable to any broad risk-off from US-Canada escalation spiral post Sept 8.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol elevated. NZD defensive in commodity-bloc risk-off episodes.
implications.GBP: GBPCAD directional trade on CAD weakness. GBP otherwise dominated by BoE path and Jackson Hole/Warsh USD dynamics this week.
implications.JPY: Safe-haven JPY bid in any risk-off commodity-bloc shock. CADJPY lower on dual CAD weakness and structural JPY bid from BOJ Sep hike cycle.

themes.watchLevel: USDCAD 1.4248 (Jun 24-30 high, MNI bull trigger) is the primary topside target if 1.4100 breaks cleanly — this is now the base-case directional target for the tariff-war regime. USDCAD 50-day EMA near 1.4017-1.4021 is the critical downside support; a clear break would signal deeper corrective retracement and requires a surprise diplomatic development. Sept 8 Canada retaliation effective date: if US counter-retaliates (Greer signalled this possibility), USDCAD accelerates toward 1.4248+; if US absorbs without response, some near-term CAD relief possible. Specific product list (HTS lines) publication in coming days is the next information event — broader/more aggressive list than signalled = further CAD pressure; narrower/targeted = modest relief. Formal re-opening of US-Canada talks = theme shifts back toward negotiation premium (currently the tail risk given USTR 'no new talks planned' statement). Section 338 has no statutory expiry — tariffs stay until the President modifies or terminates; timeline for resolution now open-ended and structurally bearish for CAD.

themes.title: Japan-US joint FX intervention regime + BOJ Sep hike ~80% priced — USDJPY ~159, Himino speech Aug 27 and Tokyo CPI Aug 28 are live near-term catalysts ahead of Sep 17-18 BOJ meeting
themes.summary: As of August 24, USDJPY is trading just above 159.00 with the joint intervention regime nominally intact but untested for over three weeks since the initial ~$59B operation at end-July drove USDJPY to 155.27. The yen has surrendered most of its intervention gains, with USDJPY rising approximately 0.89% during August overall, as carry traders rebuilt short-JPY positions in the absence of follow-up intervention. BOJ September 17-18 meeting remains the primary hard catalyst, with OIS swaps pricing approximately 80% probability of a 25bp hike to 1.25%. The central debate has now shifted from whether the BOJ hikes to whether Tokyo can persuade markets that 1.25% is the beginning of a more meaningful tightening cycle rather than another incremental step while the rate differential with the US remains wide. Two major near-term catalysts emerge this week: (1) BOJ Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino speaks on Thursday August 27, kicking off a series of public BOJ appearances before the September 17-18 decision — his remarks will be scrutinized for any validation or pushback against aggressive September hike pricing, though he is not expected to pre-commit to a specific path; (2) Tokyo CPI for August is released Friday August 28 — coming off July's national CPI at approximately 2.0% YoY headline, a firm Tokyo print would harden September hike bets and press USDJPY toward its 200-day average. BOJ Governor Ueda is unlikely to speak at Jackson Hole itself but is expected at a G20 gathering in the US the following week, where he may provide additional signalling. The intervention regime's credibility is being tested daily at current levels: three weeks without follow-up action means carry traders have largely recouped the move, and a daily close above 160.00 without any official response would constitute a significant credibility break. EURUSD near 1.1680 and AUDUSD at multi-month highs near 0.7170 reflect broad USD softness from collapsed Fed hike odds and Treasury buyback-driven yield suppression — this broad USD dynamic is supportive of the yen recovery thesis from the rate differential side.

implications.JPY: Three-pillar structural JPY support remains intact: (1) G2 intervention regime — dry powder preserved but credibility eroding with 3+ week absence of follow-up; (2) BOJ Sep hike ~80% priced via swaps, cemented by inflation data and Reuters/Kyodo sourcing; (3) Fed Sep hike odds at ~33%, rate differential narrowing from both sides. Himino speech Aug 27 is the first near-term JPY catalyst this week — hawkish tone = USDJPY pressured toward 157-158; neutral/non-committal = USDJPY drifts toward 160 test. Tokyo CPI Aug 28 (same day as Warsh): firm print = BOJ hike odds harden, USDJPY drops; soft print = modest yen selling.
implications.USD: USDJPY topside capped by intervention threat and ~80% Sep BOJ hike pricing. DXY softened to ~98.80-98.99 by Treasury buyback doubling. Rate differential direction of travel clearly USD-negative vs JPY from both sides narrowing simultaneously. Warsh keynote Aug 28 is the dominant USD catalyst across all pairs.
implications.EUR: EURJPY under pressure from intervention mechanism and BOJ hike pricing. EURUSD near 1.1680, capped below 1.1700, remains primarily a USD story keyed to Jackson Hole.
implications.GBP: GBPJPY under dual intervention and carry-unwind pressure. GBPUSD supported by UK July CPI 2.9% YoY and broad USD weakness.
implications.CHF: CHFJPY lower on intervention pressure. USDCHF under pressure from broad USD softness. SNB in easing mode.
implications.CAD: CADJPY lower on dual pressure: CAD structural weakness from Section 338 tariff war + JPY structural bid from BOJ hike cycle.
implications.AUD: AUDJPY under intervention pressure. AUDUSD at multi-month highs near 0.7170 supported by USD softness. Aug 27: RBA minutes release; Aug 28 (Wednesday AEST): Australia monthly CPI including trimmed mean — key RBA input.
implications.NZD: Same dynamic as AUD. NZDJPY under intervention pressure; NZDUSD benefits from broad USD softness and low Sep Fed hike odds.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY 160.00 is the immediate critical level — a daily close above 160 without official verbal or actual intervention signals carry traders have overpowered the regime; 3+ weeks since last intervention makes this risk non-trivial. USDJPY below 157.50 = intervention credibility reasserting. USDJPY below 155.27 (post-intervention low) = regime decisively winning. Himino speech Aug 27: hawkish validation of Sep hike = USDJPY pressured 157-158; neutral = drifts toward 160. Tokyo CPI Aug 28: firm above 2.0% = hike bets harden; soft miss = modest yen selling. BOJ Sep 17-18 meeting is the hard binary: hike to 1.25% = USDJPY likely drops toward 155-152, intervention burden reduces; no hike = JPY sells off sharply, 160+ re-test, intervention regime faces acute stress. Ueda at G20 next week: any explicit guidance beyond Himino's framing is an additional catalyst. Warsh dovish/framework JH speech Aug 28 = USDJPY three-pillar bearish case fully reinforced. Any MoF/Bessent statement disclaiming further intervention = theme ends immediately.

themes.title: Warsh Jackson Hole keynote Aug 28 10am ET — dominant USD binary THIS WEEK; PCE + Q2 GDP revision Aug 26 are pre-keynote data risks; Sep hike odds ~33%; DXY ~98.80-98.99 softened by Treasury buyback doubling
themes.summary: As of August 24, the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium opens in three days (August 27-29), with Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's keynote address at 10:00am ET on Friday August 28 as the dominant USD macro event of the week. The full schedule will not be released until 8pm ET Thursday August 27. DXY is trading near 98.80-98.99, its lowest since mid-May, having weakened further during the prior week primarily driven by the US Treasury's announcement that it would at least double its bond buyback program to at least $32 billion per quarter starting early September — a structural yield-suppression move that pulled longer-dated Treasury yields lower and weighed on the dollar even as Friday's US flash composite PMI printed a 52-month high of 56.0. EURUSD ended the prior week near 1.1680, capped below 1.1700. AUDUSD climbed to multi-month highs near 0.7170. Gold surged to a three-month peak above $4,600. Pre-keynote data risks on Wednesday August 26 include July PCE (core and headline), Q2 GDP second estimate, durable goods, personal income, and personal spending — all at 8:30am ET. September Fed hike odds remain near 33% (one-in-three), little changed from the prior week's ~30.6%, driven by: the July FOMC's unusual 9-3 vote to hold at 3.50-3.75% (Logan, Hammack, and Kashkari dissenting for immediate hike); hawkish FOMC minutes released August 19 ('many policymakers believe further rate increases could become necessary'); weak July retail sales (first monthly decline in nine months); July CPI at 3.4% YoY; and softening employment data. Governor Christopher Waller has also signalled openness to tightening if price data does not moderate. Warsh has given deliberately evasive answers at both press conferences and told reporters after July 29 that the speech will aim to 'frame big picture questions,' describing it as 'a blank piece of paper.' The symposium theme is 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy,' which some analysts argue provides structural cover for a framework-only speech that sidesteps near-term policy signals — itself a de facto dovish outcome given current pricing. This week also features BOJ Deputy Governor Himino speaking Thursday August 27 at Jackson Hole, Australia monthly CPI Wednesday, and the RBA minutes Tuesday — all potential cross-currency catalysts surrounding the Warsh event. September 11 CPI (August data) is the next major US data event post-Jackson Hole. The September 16 FOMC with updated SEP/dot plot is the hard policy event.

implications.USD: DXY ~98.80-98.99 — at multi-month lows from collapsed Sep hike odds (33%), yield-suppression from Treasury buyback doubling, and data miss trio. Jackson Hole Aug 28 is the week's primary tiebreaker: hawkish Warsh (signals Sep hike still on table, pushes odds above 50%) = DXY recovers 100-150 pips toward 99.50-100.50, EURUSD pulls back toward 1.1350-1.1450; framework/structural speech (no policy signal, reads as de facto dovish) = USD weakness extends, DXY tests toward 97.50-98; explicitly dovish = EURUSD retests 1.17+, DXY toward 96-97. Pre-keynote PCE/GDP data Aug 26 is the immediate risk: a hot PCE surprise above 3.0% core would independently lift hike odds and USD before Warsh speaks.
implications.JPY: Dovish or framework JH = USDJPY three-pillar bearish case (intervention + BOJ hike + Fed hold) fully reinforced, 155-157 test likely. Hawkish JH = rate differential modestly restored, USDJPY back toward 160 but intervention threat still caps. Tokyo CPI also Friday Aug 28 — dual catalysts on the same day.
implications.EUR: EURUSD near 1.1680, capped below 1.1700. ECB at approximately 2.40% vs Fed at 3.50-3.75%; narrowing rate differential from Fed side is EUR-positive. Hawkish Warsh = EURUSD pulls back toward 1.1350-1.1450; framework/dovish = EURUSD retests 1.17+. Domestic calendar offers little before Friday's Jackson Hole — pair is almost entirely a USD/rate differential story this week.
implications.GBP: GBPUSD near 3-month highs, supported by UK July CPI 2.9% YoY and broad USD weakness. BoE cutting cycle limits GBP outperformance vs EUR but maintains GBP bid vs USD on diverging rate paths. Two-way risk around JH keynote Aug 28.
implications.CAD: Treasury buyback-driven USD softness provides USDCAD compressing headwind but Section 338 tariff regime (50% live since Aug 22) and Sept 8 Canada retaliation dominate USDCAD directional bias. Structural trend remains bullish; post-retaliation clarity, Fed theme reasserts for USDCAD medium-term direction.
implications.AUD: AUDUSD at multi-month highs near 0.7170. RBA minutes Aug 25 and Australia monthly CPI Aug 27 (Wednesday) are domestic catalysts — trimmed mean inflation is the key RBA input. USD softness is primary driver. AUDUSD near 50-day EMA at ~0.7011 (already pierced), technically constructive. Sensitive to Canada trade war risk-off contagion.
implications.NZD: RBNZ same dynamic as RBA. NZDUSD benefits from broad USD softness and low Sep hike odds. Sensitive to Canada trade war risk-off contagion.
implications.CHF: SNB in easing mode; USDCHF under pressure from broad USD weakness and Treasury yield suppression. CHF safe-haven bid provides additional support in risk-off episodes around JH volatility and Canada escalation.

themes.watchLevel: Pre-keynote data Aug 26: July core PCE above 3.0% or Q2 GDP upside surprise = independent USD lift, hike odds spike before Warsh speaks; in-line/soft = status quo, full focus shifts to Aug 28 keynote. Warsh keynote Aug 28 10am ET is the PRIMARY binary: hawkish (Sep hike explicitly on table, odds above 50%) = DXY recovers 100-150 pips, EUR/USD below 1.1450, AUDUSD below 0.7000; framework/structural speech (no policy signal, de facto dovish by default) = USD weakness extends, DXY tests 97.50-98; explicitly dovish = EUR/USD retests 1.17+, DXY toward 96-97. DXY closing and sustaining below 97.00 = hawkish narrative fully broken. DXY sustaining above 100.50 = hawkish repricing fully underway. Sep 11 CPI (August data) is next major US data event post-JH. Sep 16 FOMC with updated SEP/dot plot is the hard policy event — the real tiebreaker between the current market split.
